name: DNSSEC Checker
description: Check whether a domain has DNSSEC enabled and inspect its chain of trust.

hints.domain: Give the domain to inspect; the check needs network access to query DS and DNSKEY records.
hints.output: The chain of trust walks up from the domain, at most three levels, and reports whether each level publishes a DS record.

faq.q: How do DS records and DNSKEY differ?
faq.a: A DS record points the parent zone's trust anchor at the child zone, while the DNSKEY is the child's own public key; both are needed for DNSSEC to count as enabled.

faq.q: Does a missing DS record mean there is no DNSSEC?
faq.a: Not necessarily, the parent zone may not be signed at all; the domain's own signatures are still detected.

faq.q: Why can the result differ from real resolution?
faq.a: The check goes through the system resolver, whose cache and path may differ; DNSSEC validation failures usually happen on the recursive server side.
